beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: MRP-VM asks why one excellent research answer may disappear on the next request.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its opening thought experiment compares a brilliant theory assessment with a shallow repeat.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers learn to preserve the procedure, sources, tests, and authority behind recurring work.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The proposed architecture gives those responsibilities a versioned home around powerful models.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An improvement remains a candidate until evaluation and publication authorize a new active version.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The first comparison identifies decisive disagreements between two theories and suggests an experiment.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A week later, a similar request produces a weaker comparison without an explainable cause.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An Agentic Knowledge Unit gives the procedure, sources, tests, and interpreter a maintained identity.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That structure makes changes inspectable when another request arrives under a recorded configuration.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Repeatability still requires varied tests, including cases where that procedure should stay inactive.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Operational feedback can motivate a candidate revision without changing the active procedure immediately.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The proposed process compares candidates against baselines and checks for regressions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Proposal, evaluation, approval, and activation remain separate responsibilities.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Published versions retain a coherent identity and a target for rollback.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book uses these distinctions to connect improvement with control over consequential change.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Start with the gap between a good answer and a repeatable organizational practice.
